claims.text: Ab initio calculations predict that atomic-scale configurational entropy and vacancy formation energy govern the structural and chemical stability of high-entropy nanoalloys at high temperature.
Optimizing atomic-scale configurational entropy reduces vacancy formation energy.
Reduced vacancy formation energy improves structural and chemical stability.
A nanoalloy with optimized configurational entropy will have greater thermal stability than a non-optimized baseline.
A nanoalloy with optimized configurational entropy will have greater radiation resistance than a non-optimized baseline.
A nanoalloy with optimized configurational entropy will have improved mechanical properties relative to a non-optimized baseline.
The prediction applies over a temperature range of 500–1000 °C.
The prediction applies to compositions ranging from equiatomic to non-equiatomic high-entropy nanoalloys.
